title: Why do you watch movies/shows, apart from only for entertainment?

commenti.body: Hey there Better_Fun525 - thanks for saying thanks! TheGratitudeBot has been reading millions of comments in the past few weeks, and you’ve just made the list!

**What exactly do you mean by this I didn't get it** : I mean I am putting my answers for Feature films. Documentaries I have not seen much \[at all\] to comment

**I can understand, movies can be a way for escapism, so not so hard to accept** : Thanks. I am talking about escaping reality being a reason for watching films

>And consider my answer for Features only 

What exactly do you mean by this I didn't get it.

>Hard to accept] To manage/handle emotion

I can understand, movies can be a way for escapism, so not so hard to accept

>never watch films to learn anything

So far what I have seen and from my personal experience,  you really can't learn anything to its fullest through a movie. But you can experience it, to get a gist, or become aware of the same.

Mostly it is entertainment, so just thinking aloud the other reasons

* To give company to someone
* \[Hard to accept\] To manage/handle emotion
* To understand and enjoy the Honest Trailer of it
* To understand and enjoy its HISHE
* As a hang out medium/Party

\_\_\_\_\_

\* I never watch films to learn anything. And consider my answer for Features only \[Documentaries are entirely uncharted for me\], as I replied to you same question somewhere else :P
I have ADHD. My brain is like a hamster on a wheel. I watch movies for all the reasons other do, but I also watch movies and TV just to get a break from my brain.
Coping mechanism.
[removed]

I like documentaries. I suggest *The Imposter* and *Exit Through the Gift Shop*. 

Also *Evil Genius* and on Netflix is really good.
For the enrichment of my life ✨

I would definitely say that most of my watching is not for "entertainment" but rather for gaining aesthetic/emotional/intellectual knowledge, similar to how other arts work, especially literature, I'm guessing. But I don't read (at least not right now) and film is a good enough (and easier to understand) replacement for me.  

Shoutout to Cronenberg for adapting Delillo's Cosmopolis!
I was already on board with your eloquent comment and then you really sold me completely at the end.

To Kill a Mockingbird. It taught me that there are three sides to every story: yours, mine, and the truth. And without attempting to ascertain the other party’s perception, you’ll never fully know the truth of a situation.

Sometimes I will watch a movie from past decades to see a snapshot of life at the time. .... or at least the director's understanding of life at that time. 

For example, Goldie Hawn's first movie was Cactus Flower. She was supposed to be a hippie, but the middle aged guys who wrote the movie had no idea what hippies were like. It is very entertaining. 

OTOH, the opening scene of Taking Of Pelham 123 is a throw away scene, with an actress you never see again in the movie. She has lost her wedding ring down sink and a plumber has been call. Our main character mutters, "we've only let em on the job a month ago and they've been nothing but trouble".  I'm sure this is the actual feeling of the writer or director about women in the work place.

For me once I’ve seen something it’s a kind of comfort in company/familiarity to return to it. There are several films I’ve put on 50-100 times.  The presence of certain sentiments in daily life can be very significant –like listening to your favourite music

For the emotional release. I get emotionally invested in movies and show I love and when something happens to them, I feel it and it is good for me. Happy when they are happy, sad when they are sad. Very few shows/movies do it to me though. That's not true. A ton of them do...
Sometimes this ^^ especially if the kids are watching the show
To be educated on the message

>Art, in other words, can truly reveal the purpose of life.

Can you suggest some movies like that and which movies did that to you and how ?

We come to this place… for magic.
We come to the movies to laugh, to cry, to care.

Because we need that, all of us,
that indescribable feeling we get when the lights begin to dim.
And we go somewhere we’ve never been before;
not just entertained, but somehow reborn.
Together.

Dazzling images, on a huge silver screen.
Sound that I can feel.
Somehow, heartbreak feels good in a place likе this.
Our heroes feel like thе best part of us, and stories feel perfect and powerful.
Because here, they are.

Because a great film is proof that justice isn't arbitrary, and much more than a treat at the end of a day well lived they're fuel for a day of righteous living tomorrow.

Also, sometimes there's titties.
